title: 有的…有的…: some … others …
summary: Lets you split a group into parts, as in 有的人喝茶，有的人喝咖啡.
explanation:
有的 means 'some (of them)'. Put it before a noun at the start of the sentence: 有的人喜欢猫 'Some people like cats.' Repeat it to contrast groups: 有的人喝茶，有的人喝咖啡 'Some drink tea, others drink coffee.'

The second noun can be dropped when it's clear: 有的学生去，有的不去. 有的 always comes before the verb, never after it.

examples.zh: 有的人喝茶，有的人喝咖啡。
examples.en: Some people drink tea; others drink coffee.
Some students are going, others aren't.

examples.zh: 我的朋友有的在中国，有的在美国。
examples.en: Some of my friends are in China, some in America.

examples.zh: 这些书有的很贵，有的很便宜。
examples.en: Some of these books are expensive, some cheap.

mistakes.why: 有的 goes before the noun.
有的 + noun normally goes at the front of the sentence, before the verb.

exercises.en: Some children like singing; others like reading.
why: Correct: 有的…有的… contrasts two groups.
都 means 'all', which doesn't fit 'some … others'.
也 means 'also'; it doesn't make a second group.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'Some of my classmates are Chinese'?
options: 我的同学有的是中国人。
我的同学是有的中国人。
有的是我的同学中国人。
why: Correct: group + 有的 + 是 + noun.
有的 must come before the verb 是.

exercises.why: 有的 + noun first, then the verb.

why: Correct: 有的 + noun replaces 都.
Don't use 有的 and 都 together.
都 and 有的 contradict each other.

options: 这些苹果有的很大，有的很小。
这些苹果很大有的，很小有的。
有的这些苹果很大，很小。
why: Correct: 有的 before each description.
有的 goes before, not after.
The second group needs its own 有的.
